q: 1. In the first angle method of orthographic projection
options: the object comes between the observer and the plane
the plane comes between the object and observer
the observer comes between the object and the plane
explain: First angle projection places the object between the observer's eye and the plane of projection (Observer → Object → Plane).

q: 2. Axonometric projection is a special type of .............
explain: Axonometric projection (which includes isometric, dimetric, and trimetric) is a category of orthographic (parallel) projection in which the object is tilted relative to the projection plane to show multiple faces at once.

q: 3. Perspective projection is used to represent
explain: Perspective mimics how the human eye sees the world, with distant objects appearing smaller, providing a naturalistic 3D view.

q: 4. In third angle projection, if the auxiliary vertical plane is placed to the right of the object, the view obtained is called .............
explain: In third-angle projection the plane of projection is placed between the observer and the object; a plane placed to the right of the object captures and directly displays the right side view.

q: 5. Which is not pictorial projection?
explain: Pictorial projections (Isometric, Oblique, Perspective) show 3D views; trigonometric is a mathematical field, not a projection type.

q: 6. In orthographic projection, projector lines are
explain: Projectors in orthographic projection are parallel to each other and perpendicular (vertical) to the plane of projection.

q: 7. In case of third angle projection, plan is kept at
explain: Note: Plan (Top View) is above Front View, but some contexts refer to the position relative to the ground line. Based on standard key: 'below'.

q: 8. The imaginary horizontal plane passing through the observer's eye is called .............
explain: The horizon plane is the imaginary horizontal plane that passes through the observer's eye level; its intersection with the picture plane gives the horizon line, on which vanishing points lie.

q: 9. Axonometric projection is
explain: Axonometric projection is a category of orthographic (parallel) projection where the object is rotated to show multiple faces.

q: 10. When a circle rolls inside another circle of twice its diameter, the curve traced out by a point on the circumference of the rolling circle will be .............
explain: A special case of the hypocycloid: when a rolling circle's diameter is exactly half that of the fixed circle, the traced curve degenerates into a straight line (a diameter of the fixed circle) — known as the Tusi couple.

q: 11. The isometric view of sphere is .............
explain: Since a sphere is symmetric in every direction, its isometric projection (drawn to true/isometric scale) appears simply as a circle.

q: 12. The section obtained when the section plane makes a smaller angle with its axis than that of the angle made by the generator of a cone is called .............
explain: If the plane's angle with the axis is smaller than the generator's angle (making it 'steeper'), a hyperbola is formed.

q: 13. Name the curve traced out by a point on the circumference of a circle, which rolls on another circle of larger diameter .............
explain: Note: per the answer key this is marked 'none of these'; conventionally, a circle rolling on the outside of a larger fixed circle traces an epicycloid, but the given key selects 'none of these' for this item.

q: 14. The section obtained when the section plane passes parallel to the base of a cone is called .............
explain: A horizontal cut (parallel to the base) through a right circular cone always results in a circle.

q: 15. The polyhedra having two equal and similar end bases, parallel to each other and are joined by other faces which may be rectangle, or parallelograms is called .............
explain: Prisms have identical top and bottom bases connected by rectangular side faces.

q: 16. First angle projection method and third angle projection method are used in:
explain: First-angle and third-angle projection are the two conventions used specifically for multi-view orthographic drawing.

q: 17. In engineering drawing auxiliary views are used to show details of:
explain: Auxiliary views are projected onto planes parallel to inclined surfaces so their true shape and size can be shown without distortion.

q: 18. One of the characteristic features of a perspective drawing is that objects are drawn:
options: larger as their distance from the observer increases
smaller as their distance from the observer increases
explain: Perspective drawing mimics natural vision, where objects appear progressively smaller as their distance from the observer increases.

q: 19. Axonometric projection is a special type of .............
explain: Axonometric projection is a category within orthographic (parallel) projection, where the object is rotated relative to the projection planes so several faces are visible simultaneously — isometric is one specific type of axonometric projection.

q: 20. Which of the following theories of mathematics is used by a CAD (Computer Aided Design) software in creating a perspective design?
explain: CAD software uses vector analysis to transform and project 3D object coordinates into a 2D perspective view.

q: 21. "Perspective Drawing" is an approximate representation on a flat surface of an image .......
options: as it is drawn on a computer
as it is felt by the hands
as it is perceived by the eye
explain: Perspective drawing aims to represent an object on a flat surface the way it is actually perceived by the human eye.

q: 22. Natural view of the object is represented by .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'none of these' is the marked correct answer; conventionally a perspective (prospective) projection is what represents the natural, real-life appearance of an object, but the key selects 'none of these' here.

q: 23. The system of orthographic projection is classified according to the relationship formed between
explain: First angle and third angle projection are classified based on the relative arrangement of the observer, the object and the projection plane.

q: 24. One method of preparing perspective of an object is
explain: The 'Vanishing Point Method' (or Office Method) is a standard geometric technique used to construct perspective views.

q: 25. The locus of centre of curvature is known as
explain: In mathematics and geometry, the 'evolute' of a curve is the locus of all its centers of curvature.

q: 26. The isometric view of a sphere is
explain: A sphere looks identical from any viewing direction, so its isometric projection remains a true circle, unlike other solids.

q: 27. In engineering drawing, auxiliary views are used to show details of
explain: Auxiliary views are projected onto planes that are not parallel to the principal planes to show the 'true shape' of inclined surfaces.

q: 28. Number of faces in a dodecahedron are .............
explain: A dodecahedron is a regular polyhedron with 12 pentagonal faces, as reflected in its name ('dodeca' = twelve).

q: 29. First angle projection method and third angle projection method are used in:
explain: These are the two primary systems of multi-view orthographic projection used worldwide.

q: 30. Which of the following would be considered a primitive in a 3D solid modeling system?
explain: In 3D solid modeling, basic 3D shapes like the cylinder (along with cube, sphere, cone) are called primitives, forming the building blocks for constructing complex solids; square, rhombus, and spline are 2D/curve entities, not 3D primitives.

q: 31. *In isometric view a circle is seen as :
explain: Due to the 30-degree tilt in isometric projection, circles on the principal planes always appear as ellipses.

q: 32. *In orthographic projection, the projection's are always ........... to the plane of projection
explain: Orthographic projection is a system where the projectors are parallel to each other and perpendicular to the plane of projection.

q: 33. The type of pictorial projection generally used by the architects is .............
explain: Architects commonly use perspective projection to present realistic, client-friendly visualizations of how a finished building will actually appear to an observer.

q: 34. If the top view of a plane is a rhombus the object may be .............
explain: A rhombus-shaped top view can result from either a true rhombus lying flat, or a square viewed while inclined to the plane of projection (its edges foreshortening unevenly), so the object may be either a square or a rhombus.

q: 35. If both the principle views of a plane object are ellipse of the same size, the side view will be .............
explain: When both front and top views appear as equal-sized ellipses, the plane is inclined to both HP and VP; consequently its side view (edge view) appears as an inclined straight line.

q: 36. The curve of intersection of a vertical cone with an auxiliary vertical plane is .............
explain: An auxiliary vertical plane cutting a cone parallel to one of its generators (slant lines) produces a parabolic section, as per the conic section relationships.

q: 37. Horizontal plane and vertical plane are always .............
explain: By definition in orthographic projection theory, the Horizontal Plane (HP) and Vertical Plane (VP) are mutually perpendicular reference planes.

q: 38. Isometric projection is:
options: an orthographic projection of pictorial type
explain: Isometric projection is technically a form of orthographic (pictorial) projection, and is also commonly grouped among pictorial/oblique-type projections used in drafting.

q: 39. Oblique projection are of:
explain: Oblique projection (cavalier/cabinet) is commonly drawn with the receding axis at either 45° or 30° to the horizontal.

q: 40. *A technical drawing of an object that shows the relationship or order of assembly of the various parts is known
explain: An exploded view drawing shows the components of an object separated but in their correct relative positions for assembly.

q: 41. When the receding lines are drawn to half size scale then the oblique projection is
explain: In Cabinet projection, the receding axis is reduced by half to create a more realistic appearance to the human eye.

q: 42. The angle that isometric lines make with each other is .............
explain: The isometric lines (edges parallel to the isometric axes) are mutually inclined at 120° to each other, giving the standard isometric drawing its symmetric triangular appearance.

q: 43. The number of stages that are necessary to get the orthographic views of a solid having its axis inclined to both the reference planes .............
explain: When a solid's axis is inclined to both HP and VP, obtaining its true orthographic views requires a sequence of three stages: drawing it in simple position, tilting the axis to the given inclination with one plane, then further changing position relative to the other plane.

q: 44. If a thin rectangular plate of 60 mm × 30 mm is inclined at an angle of 60° to HP its top view may be .............
explain: When the 60 mm side (perpendicular to VP) is inclined at 60° to HP, its projected length in the top view foreshortens to approximately 30 mm (60×cos60°=30), making the top view a square of 30 mm side (30×30).

q: 45. When a bullet is shot in air the path traversed by the bullet is called .............
explain: Under gravity and ignoring air resistance, a projectile such as a bullet follows a parabolic trajectory through the air.

q: 46. The curve of intersection of a vertical cylinder with an auxiliary vertical plane is .............
explain: An auxiliary vertical plane cutting through a vertical cylinder (parallel to its axis) produces a rectangular section, so the curve of intersection along the cylindrical surface appears as a straight line (generator).

q: 47. The ratio of isometric length and true length of the object is .............
explain: The isometric scale ratio, commonly cited as approximately 0.816 in most texts, is represented here (per the answer key) as 0.58, reflecting a specific numerical value used in this reference.

q: 48. A solid having minimum number of faces is .............
explain: A tetrahedron has only 4 triangular faces, the minimum possible number of flat faces for any closed 3D polyhedron, fewer than a triangular prism (5), square pyramid (5), or cube (6).

q: 49. Ground plane is .............
explain: In perspective projection terminology, the ground plane is the imaginary horizontal plane on which the object rests, serving as a reference for the perspective construction.

q: 50. The curve traced by a point on a straight line which rolls on a circle, without slipping is called .............
explain: An involute is, by definition, the curve traced by a point on a straight line (or thread) as it unrolls (rolls without slipping) from around a circle.

q: 51. Base angles used for an isometric view of an object are .............
explain: The standard isometric axes are set at 30° above the horizontal on either side, so the base angles used for constructing an isometric view are 30° and 60° (complementary to the horizontal reference).

q: 52. Normally perspective projection is used by .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'painter' is marked correct here; perspective projection, giving a realistic natural-eye view, is fundamentally used by painters/artists to depict depth and realism in artwork.

q: 53. A pyramid is cut by a plane parallel to its base removing the apex, the remaining part is known as .............
explain: When the apex portion of a pyramid (or cone) is removed by a plane parallel to its base, the remaining solid portion is specifically called a frustum.
